site.name: Ajax Mica Mine
site.location: Floyd Hill area, Clear Creek County
overview: The Ajax Mica Mine, also documented as the Floyd Hill Mica Mine, is a historic mica operation in the Clear Creek pegmatite district. Federal records identify discovery in 1875 and first production in 1895; the property was initially worked for mica used in stove manufacture and was reopened during World War II-era demand in 1944.

timeline.text: USGS mineral records list discovery of the Ajax Mica Mine in 1875.
USGS records list the first production year as 1895.
The mine was reopened under Ralph D. Naslund and George Baer and produced scrap, mine-run, punch, and sheet mica.
A federal examination documented the Ajax workings and pegmatite geology on the north side of Clear Creek.

moreHistory: USGS descriptions document a zoned pegmatite with quartz, albite, and muscovite, including concentrations of sheet mica. Published workings include a shallow open cut, an adit, and an inclined shaft; separate federal surveys recorded somewhat different measurements, so the records are best read as period descriptions rather than a single exact total.

A 1944 reopening produced 50,900 pounds of scrap mica, 22,927 pounds of mine-run mica, and 1,036 pounds of full-trimmed punch and sheet mica. The mine is also associated with beryl and other pegmatite minerals.
